scene.speaker: nova
scene.bubble: For the Trades project, learn how things are made — and how to use the passive to describe a process.
scene.intro: The heart of the Inspiring Nordic project is Trades: understanding how real things are made. In this unit you read Liam's report from a guitar workshop, you learn the passive voice — the grammar we use to describe a process when the action matters more than the person — and you describe how something is made yourself. Real things are made with skill, time and care. Let's find out how.

activities.title: Reading — a report from the workshop

data.title: How a guitar is made
data.author: liam
data.text:
For our Inspiring Nordic Trades project, my group visited a small workshop where guitars are made by hand. It was amazing to see how a simple piece of wood is turned into a musical instrument.

First, the wood is chosen very carefully. Only dry, strong wood is used, because wet wood is easily damaged. Then the pieces are cut and shaped by machine, but the most important parts are still done by hand.

Next, the body of the guitar is glued together and left to dry for several days. After that, it is painted and polished until it shines. Finally, the strings are added and the guitar is tested. If a note sounds wrong, the guitar is checked again.

The maker told us that a good guitar is never made quickly. “Each instrument is built with patience,” she said. “If it is made well, it will be played for fifty years.”

Our group learned an important lesson for the Trades project: real things are made with skill, time and care — not by machines alone.

data.title: The passive
data.intro: We use the passive when the action is more important than the person who does it, or when we don't know who does it. We form it with be + past participle.

examples.text: Each guitar is made by a craftsman.

rules: Form: be (am / is / are / was / were) + past participle: is made, was built.
Use the passive when the doer is unknown or not important: The door was opened.
Add by + person only to say who did it: It was made by a craftsman.

items.sentence: Only dry wood ___ for the body.
The guitar was built ___ a craftsman.

data.voice_note: Voz: el maestro del taller (Mr Ríos), tono explicativo.
data.script: Welcome to the Trades workshop, Grade 8. Let me explain how our chairs are made. First, the wood is measured and cut. Then the legs are joined to the seat with strong glue. After that, the chair is left to dry for two days. Next, it is painted in the school colours. Finally, every chair is checked before it is used in a classroom. Nothing is sold here; everything is made for our school.

activities.title: Speaking — describe a process. In pairs, then record it.

data.text: In pairs, describe how something is made or done, using the passive. Model: “How is bread made?” — “First, the flour is mixed with water. Then it is baked in an oven.” Choose one: how bread is made, how a house is built, or how your favourite dish is cooked. Explain three or four steps, then record it.

homework.prompt: Write a short 'how it's made' text (6–8 sentences) for the Inspiring Nordic Trades blog. Choose a product (a chair, a cake, a poster…) and describe how it is made, using the passive (is made, is cut, is painted…). Capital letters and full stops!
